what:
TWO THINGS, and the second is why the first went unnoticed. (1) A CLEAN SUPERVISOR FIRING COSTS $27.39, NOT THE ~$7.40 EVERY DECISION HAS BEEN WEIGHED AGAINST. PI-20260923-JN54P2HH-0001 states plainly that the only figure on record is from a firing that also hit a separate defect and went off-mandate -- an upper bound on a MIS-WIRED firing -- and that nobody had measured a clean one. MEASURED 2026-09-24: the 06:43:42Z firing of trig_01LFo98oHRUBpoMA6H9ra2QP was clean (step-1 verification passed, lane_reconcile run, 0 authorised, 1 held, heartbeat 732c27e pushed). get_session on session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q read cost_usd $42.94 before it and $70.33 after, with nothing else in the window: $27.39, about 3.7x the number in circulation. At 4 firings/day that is ~$110/day. THE FIGURE WAS BEING USED TO ARGUE THE COST WAS SMALL.
(2) THE ROUTINE WAS STILL RUNNING AND IS INVISIBLE TO THE OBVIOUS CHECK. Reading main alone says it must be inert: neither docs/claude/work/LANE-SUPERVISOR-MANDATE.md nor the top-level `supervisor_lane` key exists on main (verified with git show origin/main:... , not assumed). But the Routine's own prompt tells it to FALL BACK to claude/e44-lane-supervisor-build, where both DO exist -- so step 1 passes and the full mandate runs, every 6 hours, off an unmerged branch. A session checking main would conclude the mechanism is safely dormant and be wrong. That is a collapsed state of the same family this repo keeps paying for: `not on main` and `not running` are different facts and the first does not imply the second.
ACTION TAKEN, not just filed: the Routine is DISABLED 2026-09-24T06:57Z, with the reason and the measured price in its own title so the next reader cannot miss it. There are currently ZERO live lanes -- the last held candidate, session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, reported COMPLETED at 05:32Z -- so it was paying ~$110/day to establish that there is nothing to watch. THE MECHANISM IS NOT BROKEN AND THIS IS NOT A CRITICISM OF IT: across its firings it correctly refused an unsafe archive in production, correctly held a lane, and correctly declined a misrouted instruction to work around permission prompts (recorded in its 06:44Z heartbeat's `unrouted`). It should be re-enabled when lanes are dispatched again -- with the real price known, which is the point of this row.
[!] ONE THING THIS ROW DOES NOT ESTABLISH: whether $27.39 is representative or whether this firing was unusually expensive. It is ONE clean firing, n=1. Two more readings would make it a figure; today it is a measurement, and it is still the only clean one there has ever been.
